name: winnow (parser combinators)
verdict_reason: parse-rosetta-rs shows winnow 1.0.1 parsing canada.json in 27ms vs 68ms for nom 8.0.0 and a 1s vs 3s debug build. But that is one number-heavy JSON file timed as whole-process wall clock, the README warns the parsers are not validated and differ in quality, the benchmark is maintained by winnow's author, and serde_json (18ms) beats both.
tier_reason: Public harness with kernel and rustc stated, but no CPU model; maintained by winnow's author.
claimed_speedup: Parse (release) 27ms vs 68ms; debug build 1s vs 3s; binary overhead 67 KiB vs 88 KiB (winnow v1.0.1 vs nom v8.0.0); serde_json 18ms
workload: Each library's example app parses nativejson-benchmark canada.json (number-heavy) once per process, timed with hyperfine; build time is a clean debug build; overhead is release binary size over a null app.
hardware: x86_64 Linux machine, CPU model not stated
one_liner: Fork of nom that parsed canada.json 2.5x faster and built 3x faster than nom 8 in its author's comparison suite.
how_it_is_fast: Parsers are Fn(&mut I) -> O rather than nom's pure Fn(I) -> (I, O), so Ok and Err values are smaller and more likely to stay in registers, and the default ContextError keeps error overhead low. winnow deliberately skips nom 8's GAT-based parser modes, so each parser is generated for one mode instead of up to eight, which cuts build time and binary size.
use_it_when: Writing new combinator parsers for text or binary formats where build time and parse speed both matter
Migrating from nom; winnow keeps nom's model and ships a migration guide
skip_it_when: Parsing JSON: use serde_json or a SIMD JSON crate, which beat both combinator libraries
You depend on nom's ecosystem (nom-locate, nom-supreme) and do not want to port
caveats: Single workload (canada.json) and whole-process timing, including startup and file reading
The README notes the parsers have not been validated and may differ in quality; the nom and winnow apps may use different float parsers
Benchmark maintained by winnow's author; no CPU model
tradeoffs: API churn: winnow's README frames it as willing to change for future parsers, unlike nom's focus on stability

evidence.quote: Parsers have not been validated and might have differing levels of quality
